To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and fabricated Janus bilayer heterostructures, which can effectively steer the charge separation for photocatalytic hydrogen production, by using the oriented assembly of two-dimensional monolayers.
we have assembled 1T MoSe2 monolayers on Bi12O17 monolayers to form a Janus bilayer, which exhibits superior visible-light hydrogen evolution activity.
Janus bilayer (Cl2)-(MoS2)-(Bi12xOy) junctions, a 2D structure different from van der Walls heterostructures, are constructed by oriented assembly of monocrystalline monolayers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of Janus bilayers by oriented assembly of monomers.
the development of a new 2-dimensional Janus bilayer structure for photocatalytic hydrogen production.
the design and synthesis of a new Janus bilayer motif and the exploration of its application in photocatalytic hydrogen production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work presents a new 2-dimensional (2D)-Janus motif and a novel strategy to steer the charge flow via atomic-level directional charge transfer in 2D Janus bilayer photocatalyst, leading to superior visible-light PCE for hydrogen evolution.
the Janus bilayer heterostructures have a superior visible light hydrogen evolution performance due to the atomic-level charge separation and flow.
the superior visible light hydrogen evolution performance of Janus bilayers is due to the atomic-level directional charge flow steering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oriented assembly of different 2D materials is a promising way to construct 2D Janus junctions, which may be used for other photocatalytic applications.
we have developed a new 2-D motif of Janus (Cl₂)-(Bi₁₂O₁₇)-(MoS₂) bilayers by oriented assembly of monolyer, which is a new 2-d motif different from van-der-waals heterostructures.

we have demonstrated that the atomic-level directional charge flow can be realized in a precise manner in 2D materials by the oriented assembly of different monolayers, which is of great significance for designing highly efficient PHE systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Janus bilayer motif can be used as an effective strategy to design efficient PHE systems.
the Janus bilayer motif, which has been overlooked, is a powerful platform for designing high-efficiency PHE systems.

the atomic-level oriented assembly of monomers can effectively steer the charge separation and transfer in 2D heterostructures, and hence endows the resultant Janus bilayer structures with a high photocatalytic activity.
